messages:
Maya: heads up — automated monitor alerted on a single host with repeated ECC correctable errors, followed by a driver reset. Seeing increased 500s from the inference fleet.

ops-bot: INCIDENT GENERATED: GPU driver reset spike on node gpu-node-17 (XID 64/31 series). Alert level: PAGING.

Leo_oncall: I'm on it. pulling logs from gpu-node-17 now. if anyone is on-call for infra let me know. @nina_ops @carter_infra

Nina_ops: ack. i can help with node telemetry and cordon if needed. please paste `kubectl get pods -o wide` for the node.

Maya: sample from app logs: "model-infer: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = container crashed (exit status 137)" — multiple pods on that node restarted. customer errors spiked.

Leo_oncall: running `ssh jump@gpu-node-17 'dmesg | tail -n 80'` now. output shows repeated: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Class 0b, 0xce2f0` then `kernel: nvidia: GPU reported ECC error, correctable` and then `nvidia: bug: GPU hang` before driver reset.

Carter_infra: that pattern usually indicates memory subsystem noise or thermal. i'm going to cordon the node and start draining non-critical inference pods. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` -> done.

Leo_oncall: starting drain:`kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — moving pods to other nodes. routing should kick in, but watch throughput.

Maya: routing note — we're hitting fallback policy: some requests are routed to smaller model-quantized variants. latency up ~120ms p95 and error rate on the affected service is 6% (baseline 0.4%). telling support to open a customer impact note.

Deploy-bot: DEPLOYMENT NOTIFICATION: 2 pods failed restart on gpu-node-17, restarted on gpu-node-19.

Nina_ops: i've pulled NVML logs, attaching tail excerpt: `2026-03-15T09:12:02Z NVML E: ECC error detected on GPU0 (correctable). Count increments rapidly.` Also seeing elevated VRAM correctable counters.

Leo_oncall: trying safe repro: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,FB` shows FB ECC correctable increasing. running `watch -n 1 nvidia-smi` to see behavior.

Maya: customer impact classification: SLO latency degradation and increased 5xx. Not total outage, but visible degrade for customers on high-throughput endpoints. recommend severity P1-P2.

Carter_infra: opening a hardware ticket with colo vendor and scheduling node reboot after drain completes. also setting node to quarantine: label gpu-node-17 debug=quarantined.

Leo_oncall: can we mitigate for the short-term by shifting some critical traffic? Suggest moving heavy realtime routes to dedicated-capacity pool in region. @maya can you trigger route rebind?

Maya: doing a controlled reroute now — switching traffic for route /v1/generate-critical to dedicated-pool-dc-west-1, gradual 20% steps. monitoring.

Ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: /v1/generate-critical now 40% -> 60% on dedicated-pool-dc-west-1.

Nina_ops: while drain finishes, capturing kernel oops: here's the stackframe snippet pasted for triage: ```kernel: [ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID 4123: NVRM: guard page violation in GPU memory
kern: [ 12345.679012] Call Trace: dump_stack+0x45/0x5f
```

Leo_oncall: thanks. sharing log with hw team. do we have thermal telemetry? any fan speed anomalies?

Carter_infra: fans normal. ambient temp slightly high but within spec. i've ordered a live ECC counter export and will push to S3: `aws s3 cp /tmp/gpu-ecc-counters.csv s3://redwood-debug/gpu-node-17/`

Maya: support note drafted for customers who saw errors: short blurb + mitigation steps + ETA for next update. tagging product and comms to approve.

Leo_oncall: drain complete. pods evacuated. node in Quarantine. initiating reboot for a deeper hardware reset: `sudo systemctl isolate reboot.target` (will monitor rejoin).

Deploy-bot: NODE EVENT: gpu-node-17 shutdown requested by leo_oncall. migration status: 100% pods moved.

Nina_ops: after reboot, NVML still reports intermittent correctable ECC increments, but no immediate driver reset in the 12m window. capturing longer-run telemetry.

Carter_infra: vendor said they will RMA if we keep seeing resets after additional soak. opening RMA ticket.

Maya: customer comms: initial message sent. we've rolled back some traffic to dedicated pools and are monitoring. will update in 30m or when status changes.

Leo_oncall: next steps in runbook: 1) keep node quarantined 2) attach SOC logs + NVML counters to incident 3) if resets reappear, escalate to HW RMA and mark node unschedulable until replacement.

Maya: anybody seeing secondary nodes with similar pattern? quick fleet scan shows two nodes with small uptick in correctable counts but no resets yet — flags raised.

Nina_ops: good call. i've increased sampling rate for ECC counters across the fleet and added an alert threshold for spikes of >100 correctable increments/min.

Carter_infra: we'll run a controlled soak test on a spare node with synthetic workload to try to reproduce Xid pattern. will post results to incident doc.

Leo_oncall: handing off to night oncall. leaving notes: node quarantined, RMA ticket open, routing adjusted, customers notified. ping me if it flares up.

Maya: thanks everyone. tagging for visibility: @carter_infra :eyes:, @nina_ops :medal_sports: — incident status: MONITORING.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity set to P2. Last action: node quarantined and rebooted.

Maya: closing thread for now — will reopen if driver resets reoccur or customer impact increases.
